FWD-Doc is a global community of disabled creators and allies in documentary film that elevates stories by, for and about disabled people. The Jonathan Logan Family Foundation has supported FWD-Doc since its early days, including strategic planning support to help the organization get off the ground. Today, FWD-Doc builds community for its more than 1,200 members, champions disabled media makers and advocates for more inclusive, equitable and accessible practices within the entertainment industry for filmmakers and audiences.

Check out these resources from FWD-Doc:

Event Accessibility Scorecard – Providing feedback to make film festivals and other events more accessible.

Framework for Evaluating Disability Representation in Film and Media – Authentic representation of disabled people in film and media is not just about who is on screen, but also who is behind the camera, in decision-making roles and on the awards stage.

Documentary Budget Template – Guiding filmmakers on how to build accessibility into their film budgets and schedules.

Toolkit for Inclusion and Accessibility – Best practices for filmmakers and the industry.

The post FWD-Doc appeared first on Jonathan Logan Family Foundation.

The AIDS Memorial Quilt is dedicated to remembering the unique lives and stories of those lost to HIV/AIDS and is considered the largest community arts project in history. The Quilt was conceived of by activist Cleve Jones in 1985 as a means to help people understand the devastating impact of AIDS. Today, there are roughly 50,000 panels dedicated to more than 110,000 individuals in this epic 54-ton tapestry.

The Jonathan Logan Family Foundation is supporting the redigitization of the Quilt in order to ensure that it remains visible, accessible and preserved for future generations. The JLFF team visited the National AIDS Memorial warehouse in the East Bay in September 2025 to see where the Quilt is housed and meet some of the dedicated staff and volunteers who care for the Quilt. Each year, the National AIDS Memorial partners with community-based organizations across the country to display sections of the Quilt to raise greater awareness about HIV/AIDS impacting people today. Read more about the redigitization efforts here and check here to see if the Quilt is on display near you.

In 1972, Barbara Jordan became the first Southern Black woman to join Congress. The documentary film The Inquisitor by Angela Tucker chronicles Representative Jordan’s career and offers a blueprint for uniting a divided America through a turbulent political era. In a world dominated by white men, Jordan moved with deft skill, earning both their respect and their fear. Her electrifying voice and moral clarity during President Richard Nixon’s impeachment captivated the nation, earning her the moniker “The Inquisitor.”

JLFF supported the production of the film, which had its world premiere at the Tribeca Film Festival in June 2025. The film premiered on PBS in February 2026.

The post The Inquisitor appeared first on Jonathan Logan Family Foundation.

Spelman College is a historically Black women’s college founded in 1881. Located in Atlanta’s Westside neighborhood, Spelman College is home to some 2,300 students. In 2022, construction began on a new Center for Innovation & the Arts just outside the campus’ historic walls and named after President Emerita Dr. Mary Schmidt Campbell. Considered the new “front porch” of the campus, the CI&A will be home to Spelman’s thriving arts programs in dance, filmmaking, photography, theater and music, as well as a cutting-edge Innovation Lab.

The Jonathan Logan Family Foundation supported the creation of the Jonathan Logan Family Foundation Center for Documentary Film Studies within the CI&A. The Center includes a classroom named for Dr. Ayoka Chenzira, pioneering filmmaker and Professor Emerita of Art & Visual Culture at Spelman College. The CI&A had its grand opening in April 2025.

Life After is a documentary film examining the tangled web of moral dilemmas and profit motives surrounding assisted dying. Disabled filmmaker Reid Davenport uncovers shocking abuses of power while amplifying the voices of the disability community fighting for justice and dignity in an unfolding matter of life and death.

The Jonathan Logan Family Foundation provided support for Life After at multiple stages, from production to the film’s impact campaign. This gripping film challenges audiences to rethink assumptions and examine a complex issue from new angles. The film had its world premiere at the 2025 Sundance Film Festival, where it was recognized with a US Documentary Special Jury Award. Find a screening near you and learn more here.

The post Life After appeared first on Jonathan Logan Family Foundation.

Firelight Media founders Marcia Smith and Stanley Nelson believe that documentary storytelling is among the most powerful tools for artistic expression and advancing social justice. BIPOC filmmakers in particular struggle to find artistic and financial resources in the broader documentary field. Firelight Media supports the creation, distribution and impact of documentary media by and about communities of color.

The Jonathan Logan Family Foundation has supported Firelight’s William Greaves Research and Development Fund since 2020. Named for filmmaking pioneer William Greaves, the fund provides resources to mid-career nonfiction storytellers from underrepresented communities. Firelight’s support of mid-career filmmakers is unique and is key to the development of talented storytellers.

Check out the latest Greaves Fund cohort here.

The post Firelight Media appeared first on Jonathan Logan Family Foundation.

Stripped for Parts: American Journalism on the Brink tells the story of a secretive hedge fund that is plundering America’s newspapers and the journalists who are fighting back. Investigative reporter Julie Reynolds, Denver Post editorialist Chuck Plunkett and others go up against the faceless Alden Global Capital in a fight to save and rebuild local journalism across America. Director Rick Goldsmith explores who will control the future of America’s news ecosystem: hedge funds concerned only with profit, or those who see journalism as a public service essential to a healthy democracy.

The Jonathan Logan Family Foundation provided early support for Stripped for Parts, which exposes the threats faced by the American journalism ecosystem. The film received the award for Best Documentary at the 2023 United Nations Association Film Festival. Check out the trailer below and visit here to find a screening near you.

The post Stripped for Parts appeared first on Jonathan Logan Family Foundation.

The Berkeley Film Foundation nurtures, sustains and preserves the local film community in East Bay cities including Berkeley, Emeryville, El Cerrito, Albany, Richmond and Oakland. Through grants for the production, post-production and distribution of films, the Berkeley Film Foundation supports filmmakers directly and works to attract the next generation of creators. With support from the Jonathan Logan Family Foundation, the Berkeley Film Foundation launched the annual Logan Elevate Grant in 2020, which provides funding to an emerging filmmaker.

The Logan Elevate Grant recipients are:

Belly of the World by April September (2025)

Becoming Us by Eli Hiller (2024)

Finding Má by Thanh Tran (2023)

The Long Rescue by Jennifer Huang (2022)

A Thousand Pines by Sebastián Diáz Aguirre (2021)

Oaklead by Alex Bledsoe (2020)

The post Berkeley Film Foundation appeared first on Jonathan Logan Family Foundation.

In The 9 Lives of Barbara Dane, American history gets a shakeup through the story of Barbara Dane, a Bay Area-based blues/jazz/folk singer, activist, feminist, record producer and committed troublemaker. The documentary film explores narratives around 1940s Communisim, 1950s white femininity, the joy and politics of the 1960s folk scene, the 1970s GI Anti-War movement and the 1980s Iran-Contra affair. Director Maureen Gosling follows Dane’s nine-decade journey as her unbending principles guide her through notoriety, obscurity and music legend, all while accumulating a hefty FBI file.

The film had its world premiere at the Mill Valley Film Festival in October 2023. Check out the trailer below and visit here to learn more.

For more than 40 years, FRONTLINE on PBS has produced investigative journalism that questions, explains and changes our world. The program has won every major journalism and broadcasting award, including numerous Emmy and Peabody Awards. FRONTLINE reaches millions through its public television platform, and more than 300 FRONTLINE documentaries are available to watch for free online.

JLFF has supported the following FRONTLINE documentary films:

The War Cabinet by Michael Kirk (2026)
Examining the inner circle of advisors and officials behind President Trump’s expansive use of the U.S. military.

The Deal: Trump, Bukele & the Gangs of El Salvador by Juan Ravell (2026)
An examination of Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele’s deal with President Trump to imprison U.S. deportees, and what each leader stood to gain.

The Rise of RFK Jr. by Michael Kirk (2025)
The dramatic and controversial rise of Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. and how he is reshaping government and public health.

Born Poor by Jezza Neumann (2025)
A look at the realities of growing up poor in America, filmed over 14 years with kids from three families.

Trump’s Power and the Rule of Law by Michael Kirk (2025)
The high-stakes showdown between President Trump and the courts over presidential power.

Trump’s Comeback by Michael Kirk (2025)
Tracing Donald Trump’s return to the presidency and examining the defining moments of his life and career.

The Rise and Fall of Terrorgram by Tom Jennings and Annie Wong (2025)
Investigating how an online network known as Terrorgram spread extremism and violence in a global community of white supremacists.

The VP Choice: Vance vs Walz by Gabrielle Schonder (2024)
Examining the lives and views of JD Vance and Tim Walz as they run for vice president.

The Choice 2024: Harris vs. Trump by Michael Kirk (2024)
Examining the lives and characters of Kamala Harris and Donald Trump and revealing key moments that shape how they would lead America.

Democracy on Trial by Michael Kirk (2024)
Investigating the roots of the criminal cases against former President Trump stemming from his 2020 election loss.

McConnell, the GOP & the Court by Michael Kirk (2023)
Examining Republican Senator Mitch McConnell’s role in America’s polarized democracy and in pushing the judiciary to the right.

Clarence and Ginni Thomas: Politics, Power and the Supreme Court by Michael Kirk (2023)
Tracing the path to power of the Supreme Court justice and his wife and how they have reshaped American law and politics.

Lies, Politics and Democracy by Michael Kirk (2022)
Investigating American political leaders and choices they’ve made that have undermined and threatened democracy in the U.S.

Plot to Overturn the Election by Sam Black (2022)
The story of how lies about election fraud made their way to the center of American politics.

American Reckoning by Yoruba Richen and Brad Lichtenstein (2022)
Investigating the unsolved 1967 murder of a local NAACP leader in Natchez, MS, and revealing an untold story of the civil rights movement and Black resistance.

Whose Vote Counts by June Cross and Tom Jennings (2020)
Investigating allegations of voter disenfranchisement and how the pandemic could impact voter turnout.

To see what’s next on FRONTLINE, visit here

The post Frontline appeared first on Jonathan Logan Family Foundation.
